text: On Nozick's tracking account, what explains how I can know that I have hands and yet not know that I am not a handless brain in a vat?
choices: In the ordinary context 'know' expresses a less demanding relation than it does once the skeptic raises the stakes
The brain-in-a-vat scenario is simply not a relevant alternative that I am required to rule out

My belief that I have hands is sensitive—were I handless I would not so believe—whereas my belief that I am not a vatted brain is insensitive, since even as such a brain I would still believe I am not one
If I were envatted, my word 'brain' would fail to refer to real brains, so the hypothesis undermines itself
explanation: Nozick's sensitivity condition requires that in the nearest world where the believed proposition is false, the subject does not believe it. The hands-belief meets this, but the not-a-BIV belief does not (in the nearest BIV world one still believes one is not a BIV), so closure fails. Option 0 is contextualism, option 1 is Dretske's relevant-alternatives reply, and option 3 is Putnam's semantic argument—three different anti-skeptical strategies.
